logs_docs_overview_content:
The Logs page shows all API requests processed by PAAP:

- Request details: Model, provider, key used, tokens in/out
- Latency: Time taken for each request
- Cost: Calculated cost per request
- Status: Success/error indicators
- Filters: By provider, model, status, search term
logs_docs_usage_content:
Filtering logs:
- Provider: Filter by specific provider
- Model: Filter by specific model
- Status: Filter by success/error
- Search: Search in request/response content

Export:
- CSV: Download logs as spreadsheet
- JSON: Download logs as structured data

Clear Logs:
- Clear all logs (does not affect providers, keys, or models)
logs_docs_troubleshoot_content:
No logs appearing
+ Cause: No API requests made or logs were cleared
+ Fix: Make an API request through PAAP

Cost shows $0.00
+ Cause: Model pricing not configured
+ Fix: Pricing is auto-calculated from known models

Export fails
+ Cause: Too many logs for browser download
+ Fix: Use filters to reduce result set
groups_docs_overview_content:
Groups allow organizing multiple models for race-based routing:

- Race Mode: Send request to multiple providers simultaneously, use fastest response
- Round-Robin: Rotate requests across providers
- Model Chain: Fallback through models in order
groups_docs_setup_content:
1. Create a group at /groups
2. Add models from different providers
3. Configure race settings:
   - Race timeout: Max time to wait for responses
   - Race condition: Number of parallel requests
4. Use the group model in your API requests
groups_docs_troubleshoot_content:
Race always picks same provider
+ Cause: Other providers are slower or failing
+ Fix: Check provider health and latency

Group model not found
+ Cause: Group name mismatch in request
+ Fix: Use exact group name from the groups page
proxy_docs_overview_content:
The Proxy page manages proxy pools for provider connections:

- Proxy Pools: Groups of proxy servers
- Provider Assignment: Assign proxies to specific providers
- Testing: Test proxy connectivity
proxy_docs_setup_content:
1. Create a proxy pool
2. Add proxy servers (host:port format)
3. Assign the pool to providers
4. Test proxy connectivity
proxy_docs_troubleshoot_content:
Proxy connection fails
+ Cause: Proxy server unreachable or auth required
+ Fix: Check proxy server status and credentials

Requests slow through proxy
+ Cause: Proxy adds latency
+ Fix: Use proxies closer to provider endpoints
settings_docs_overview_content:
The Settings page manages global PAAP configuration:

- Language: UI language selection (6 languages)
- Data Management: Clear logs, backup/restore database
- Server Control: Restart or shutdown PAAP
settings_docs_language_content:
Supported languages:
- English (default)
- Indonesia
- 中文 (Chinese)
- 日本語 (Japanese)
- 한국어 (Korean)
- العربية (Arabic)

Language changes apply immediately. All UI text and documentation will switch to the selected language.
settings_docs_data_content:
Clear All Data:
- Deletes: Logs, cost summary, usage stats, race logs
- Preserves: Providers, keys, models, groups, settings, gateway keys

Backup Database:
- Downloads complete PAAP database as file
- Use for migration or disaster recovery

Restore Database:
- Upload a previous backup to restore
- Requires PAAP restart after restore
settings_docs_server_content:
Restart:
- Restarts PAAP server process
- Connections will be briefly interrupted
- Use after config changes

Shutdown:
- Stops PAAP server completely
- You will lose connection
- Requires manual restart (systemctl start paap)
settings_docs_troubleshoot_content:
Language not changing
+ Cause: Browser cache
+ Fix: Hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R)

Clear data does not remove providers
+ Cause: Working as designed
+ Fix: Delete providers individually at /providers

Cannot restore backup
+ Cause: Backup file corrupted or incompatible version
+ Fix: Ensure backup is from same PAAP version

Shutdown not responding
+ Cause: PAAP process already stopped
+ Fix: Use systemctl start paap to restart
compression_docs_overview_content:
Smart Compressor compresses old messages before sending to provider. Saves tokens and cost.

How it works:
- Messages are compressed sequentially (one by one)
- Recent messages (last 6) are preserved for context
- Assistant messages can be compressed in Medium/High modes
- Compression is idempotent — safe to run repeatedly
compression_docs_modes_content:
Caveman:
- Drop filler words (just, really, basically, actually)
- Drop articles (a, an, the)
- Drop hedging and pleasantries
- Keep technical substance exact
- Levels: lite (whitespace only), full (filler + whitespace), ultra (maximum compression)

Ponytail:
- Lazy senior dev discipline
- YAGNI ladder (You Aren't Gonna Need It)
- Smallest working diff
- Levels: lite, full, ultra

RTK (Rust Token Killer):
- Compress tool outputs (bash, grep, git, etc.)
- 60-90% reduction on tool output
- Levels: lite, full, ultra

Multiple modes can be active simultaneously. Format: mode:level (e.g. caveman:ultra,rtk:full)
compression_docs_injection_content:
Inject custom instructions into every API request:

- Position: Prepend (before user messages) or Append (after user messages)
- Text: Custom system prompt content
- Use cases: Enforce response format, language, tone, or domain-specific behavior

The injected text appears as a system message in the request, so the AI will follow these instructions in every response.
compression_docs_headroom_content:
Headroom is an external Python service that provides additional token compression:

- Runs on a separate port (default: 8787)
- Compresses JSON tool outputs
- Runs after RTK compression
- Small tool outputs are skipped automatically

Setup:
1. Install the Headroom Python service
2. Start it on port 8787
3. Enable the toggle on this page
4. PAAP will proxy requests through Headroom

Note: Headroom adds latency per request (typically 200-900ms). Disable if latency is more important than token savings.
compression_docs_voice_content:
When Caveman mode is active, an additional voice instruction is injected:

- Drop articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically)
- Fragments OK
- Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not implement)
- Code blocks, file paths, commands, errors, URLs: keep exact
- No decorative emoji, no narrating tool calls

This makes the AI respond in terse, efficient prose without losing technical accuracy.
compression_docs_troubleshoot_content:
No compression happening:
- Cause: Level set to 'Off'
- Fix: Set level to Lite/Medium/High

Savings too small:
- Cause: Messages too small (<50 bytes)
- Fix: Normal — small messages can't be compressed

Assistant not compressed:
- Cause: Level is Lite (tool only) or message in recent 6
- Fix: Use Medium/High, or wait for message to age out

Summary shows 0:
- Cause: Server just restarted (resets counters)
- Fix: Normal — counters reset on restart
vision_docs_overview_content:
Vision auto-routes image requests to vision-capable models. When a request contains images (base64 or URL), PAAP automatically routes it to the configured vision model chain.

Features:
- Fallback chain: Try models in order, fail over to next on error
- Drag-to-reorder: Prioritize models by dragging
- Auto-save: Changes persist immediately
- Provider+Model picker: Modal-based selection like Groups
vision_docs_setup_content:
1. Navigate to /tools/vision
2. Enable the toggle (top right)
3. Click "Add Model" to open the picker modal
4. Select a provider (e.g. Xiaomi, Google AI Studio)
5. Select a vision-capable model (e.g. mimo-v2.5, gemini-2.0-flash)
6. Click "Add" — model is saved automatically
7. Add more models for fallback chain (optional)
8. Drag models to reorder priority

Recommended vision models:
- Xiaomi: mimo-v2.5 (free tier)
- Google AI Studio: gemini-2.0-flash (free tier)
- OpenRouter: various vision models
vision_docs_troubleshoot_content:
Images not being detected
+ Cause: Images must be base64 or URL in message content
+ Fix: Ensure client sends images in OpenAI format

Vision model returns error
+ Cause: Model does not support images or API key expired
+ Fix: Check model capabilities and key status

Fallback not working
+ Cause: Only one model in chain or all models failed
+ Fix: Add more vision models to the chain

Model picker shows no providers
+ Cause: No providers configured
+ Fix: Add providers at /providers first
providers_docs_overview_content:
Providers are API services that PAAP routes requests to (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Xiaomi, OpenRouter, custom endpoints, etc.)

Each provider has:
- API Keys: Credentials to authenticate with the provider
- Models: Available AI models from the provider
- Status: Online/offline indicator
- Configuration: Base URL, auth type, provider type
providers_docs_setup_content:
Adding a provider:
1. Click "Add Provider" on the providers page
2. Select provider type (builtin or custom)
3. Enter the base URL (e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1)
4. Select auth type (API key or OAuth)
5. Add API keys in the setup page
6. Detect or manually add models

Custom provider setup:
- Base URL: The API endpoint of the provider
- Auth Type: API key (header-based) or OAuth (device code flow)
- API Key: Paste the key, it will be encrypted and stored

Builtin providers (Xiaomi, StepFun, AI Studio, OpenRouter) come pre-configured. Only API keys need to be added.
providers_docs_keys_content:
Each provider can have multiple API keys for:
- Load balancing (round-robin across keys)
- Failover (if one key fails, try the next)
- Rate limit handling (rotate keys when rate limited)

Operations:
- Add Key: Paste a single API key
- Bulk Add: Paste multiple keys (one per line)
- Enable All: Enable all disabled keys
- Delete Disabled: Remove all disabled keys
- Delete All: Remove all keys
- Toggle: Enable/disable individual keys

Key naming: Keys are auto-named (key-1, key-2, etc.)
providers_docs_models_content:
Models are AI endpoints exposed by the provider (e.g. gpt-4o, claude-sonnet-4, mimo-v2.5-pro)

Operations:
- Detect Models: Auto-discover available models from the provider API
- Add Model: Manually add a model by name
- Remove Model: Delete a model from the list
- Delete All: Remove all models
- Toggle: Select/deselect models for routing

Only selected models will be available for API routing.
providers_docs_playground_content:
Test API calls directly from the setup page:
1. Select a key from the dropdown
2. Select a model
3. Enter a prompt
4. Click "Run Test"

The playground sends a real API request and shows the response, latency, and token usage.
providers_docs_troubleshoot_content:
Provider shows offline
+ Cause: All API keys are disabled or expired
+ Fix: Add a new key or re-enable existing keys
+ Verify: Check key status in the setup page

Models not detected
+ Cause: Provider API does not support model listing
+ Fix: Manually add models using the input field

OAuth connection fails
+ Cause: Device code flow expired or denied
+ Fix: Click "Connect" again to get a new code

Playground test fails
+ Cause: Invalid key, model not available, or provider error
+ Fix: Check the error message in the response

Cannot delete builtin provider
+ Cause: Builtin providers are protected from deletion
+ Fix: Disable the provider instead (toggle online off)
dashboard_docs_overview_content:
The Dashboard is the main overview page of PAAP. It displays:

- Stats Cards: Requests (24h), Tokens (24h), Cost (24h), Active Providers
- Base URL: The PAAP endpoint URL for API clients
- Gateway API Key: Manage authentication keys for clients
- Provider Topology: Visual map of all configured providers and their status
dashboard_docs_keys_content:
Gateway keys authenticate API clients (Hermes, Claude Code, etc.)

Operations:
- Generate: Create a new key with a custom name (e.g. hermes, dev, prod)
- Show/Hide: Toggle key visibility (masked by default for security)
- Copy: Copy key to clipboard for use in client configs
- Revoke: Permanently delete a key (clients using it will lose access)

Best Practices:
- Use descriptive names for keys (e.g. hermes, opencode, ci-pipeline)
- Revoke unused keys regularly
- Never share keys in public repositories
dashboard_docs_topology_content:
The topology section shows a visual map of all configured providers:

- Each node represents a provider with its status (online/offline)
- Active providers pulse green when processing requests
- Hover over a provider to see details (model count, key count, latency)
- Providers auto-refresh every 30 seconds
dashboard_docs_troubleshoot_content:
Stats show 0 requests
+ Cause: No API key configured or no client connected
+ Fix: Generate a gateway key and configure it in your client

Provider shows offline
+ Cause: API key expired or provider endpoint unreachable
+ Fix: Go to /providers/setup and check API keys
+ Verify: Click the provider to see error details

Cannot copy base URL or key
+ Cause: Browser clipboard permission denied
+ Fix: Allow clipboard access in browser settings

Gateway key not working
+ Cause: Key was revoked or mistyped
+ Fix: Generate a new key and update client config
mcp_docs_overview_content:
PAAP MCP Server provides 3 tools callable by AI agents:

- generate_image: Create images from text prompts (StepFun step-image-edit-2)
- text_to_speech: Convert text to audio/speech (StepFun step-tts-2)
- analyze_image: Analyze images using vision models

Endpoints:
- GET /mcp/status - Check MCP server status
- POST /mcp/message - JSON-RPC 2.0 (initialize, tools/list, tools/call)

Protocol: JSON-RPC 2.0
Auth: Bearer token (same as PAAP gateway key)
mcp_docs_usage_content:
Initialize MCP session:
curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/mcp/message -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}'

List available tools:
curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/mcp/message -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}'

Call text_to_speech:
curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/mcp/message -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"text_to_speech","arguments":{"text":"Hello world","voice":"Mia"}}}'

Call generate_image:
curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/mcp/message -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"generate_image","arguments":{"prompt":"a cat in space"}}}'
mcp_docs_troubleshoot_content:
Error: "method not found"
+ Cause: MCP server is not enabled
+ Fix: Enable toggle at /tools/mcp
+ Verify: curl http://localhost:9090/mcp/status

Error: "connection refused"
+ Cause: PAAP server is not running
+ Fix: sudo systemctl restart paap
+ Verify: curl http://localhost:9090/api/health

Error: "unauthorized"
+ Cause: Gateway key incorrect or missing
+ Fix: Check key at /settings > Gateway Keys
+ Verify: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer KEY" http://localhost:9090/mcp/status

Error: TTS no audio / error
+ Cause: Voice name invalid for provider
+ Fix: Check voice list per provider
+ Verify: Test via curl (see Usage Examples)

Error: Image gen timeout
+ Cause: Provider does not support image gen / API key expired
+ Fix: Check provider at /tools/mcp > Image Gen card
+ Verify: Test with different model

Error: analyze_image failed
+ Cause: Vision model not active / does not support images
+ Fix: Check fallback chain at /tools/vision
+ Verify: Test with valid image URL

MCP not visible in client
+ Cause: Config error / wrong URL
+ Fix: URL must be http://127.0.0.1:9090/mcp/message (not /api/mcp)
+ Verify: Restart client after config change

Response is slow
+ Cause: Provider model cold start latency
+ Fix: Change model at /tools/mcp card
+ Verify: Compare response times via direct curl

Audio truncated
+ Cause: Text too long / provider limit
+ Fix: Split text into smaller segments
+ Verify: Check max_tokens in provider settings
compression_docs_levels_content:
Off: No compression

Lite (batch 25): Tool outputs only
- ANSI strip, blank collapse, dedup identical lines
- Threshold: ≥50 bytes

Medium (batch 50): Tool + User + System + Assistant
- Content detection (7 types), Headroom reformat, Bloat offload
- Assistant: eligible ≥300 bytes (max Bloat Offload)
- Threshold: 50-200 (Lite pass) / ≥200 (full)

High (batch 100): All roles
- Full pipeline: Headroom + Caveman + BM25 + new strategies
- Pattern collapse, code dedup, list compaction, reasoning trim
- Threshold: 50-200 / 200-1000 / 1000+
compression_docs_features_content:
Content Detection: JSON, log, diff, code, search, HTML, text

Prose Filter: English + Indonesian filler words
- Removes: 'basically', 'actually', 'sebenarnya', 'pada dasarnya'
- Mixed language support (ID+EN in same sentence)

BM25 Extractive: Keeps most relevant segments
- Splits text into segments, scores by relevance
- Keeps top segments until target ratio

FlintChipper: Head+tail truncation
- Keeps first N lines (head) + last M lines (tail)
- Omits middle content with [... N lines omitted ...]
compression_system_prompt_desc: Text injected into every request before sending to provider
